lines: Every earlier structure in this part of the course asked the same question: where does this piece of data physically sit.
This one drops that question completely and asks something narrower instead: of everything still waiting, which one is smallest, right now.
Here's the trick worth noticing first: that tree you're picturing was never actually built anywhere.
Every parent and child position is just arithmetic on where something already sits inside one plain array.
Before the reveal, think about what actually goes wrong the moment a value lands past the very end of the array, out of order with everything above it.
Before this is a real heap again?
answer: It walks upward, one step at a time, swapping with its own parent for as long as the two are out of order, and then it stops.
A full rebuild would touch everything that's already fine. Only the one path from that new value up to the root ever needs fixing.

lines: Watch what doesn't move here, not just what does.
Every node off to the side of that one path stays exactly where it already was — the walk only ever touches its own root-ward line.
Removing the smallest value empties out the root, so something has to fill that spot immediately.
The fix is the same idea, run in the opposite direction: pull the array's own last element into the empty root, then walk it downward, swapping with whichever child is smaller, until it stops.

Here's the part that actually surprises people: build the exact same heap from the exact same elements two different ways, and the total cost changes, even though nothing about either operation changed.

Insert one at a time and you pay a walk for every single element. Sift downward from the bottom instead, and most of that walking disappears, because most nodes already sit close to the bottom, where a walk is short.
This is the one place in the whole topic where a claim gets checked against a real count instead of just argued for.
Both builds end up at a fully valid heap. Only the swap counts along the way tell you which one actually paid less.
